growing_tip.body_text: Broccoli | → Batavia → Marathon → Imperial (summer) → 2 rows per bed spaced every 18” (45 cm) on the row → Broccoli, cabbage and cauliflowers are all heavy feeders that require lots of compost, +/-1 inch (5 cm) all across the bed. In rich soils, compost can be replaced with a buried cover crop of leguminous nature, but in both cases, we add nitrogen-rich organic fertilizers like pelleted chicken manure (5-3-2) to help the plant quickly develops its canopy. → A second boost of nitrogen is added to the crop +/- 14 days after the transplant by amending the soil with blood or alfalfa meal. | For weekly supply throughout the growing season, we plant 2 different cultivars every 15 days. Each of these cultivars has a different DTM (days to maturity) which stagger the harvest window. We plant them with other heavy feeding crucifers like cauliflowers, cabbages and kohlrabi, all crops which spend +/- 60 days in the field. For summer plantings, plan for heat tolerant cultivars. → Rotary harrow → Broadfork → 30” bed prep rake + marking tubes → Declumping tray → Anti-insect net and hoops → Remove tarp and-or clean large debris. Use the rake if needed.* → Uniformly apply compost and amendments and pass with the rotary harrow at a depth of 2” (5 cm). To make transplanting easier (seeing as the soil is loose after being harrowed), we only prepare the beds when we are about to transplant. → Using the bed prep rake and 2 tubes, mark the rows both lengthways and sideways. Bring the well-watered trays. → Using the declumping tray to facilitate clump extraction, 1 person will drop the seedling while 2 others transplants the plants as fast as possible. 3 people/100’bed is good ratio for efficient workflow. → Bury the seedling all the way to where the leaves start to branch out. → Install the hoops every 5’ (1.5 m) and cover the crops with the anti-insect net. irrigation.body_text: → Drip tape or sprinkler | → Root depth: Shallow (6”-24”) → Critical period: Head development. → General: Commercial growers use 1-1-1/2” per week. Extra water during crown will add bulk to the harvest. 1
